findings.finding: Insights: For N=M+c (M huge odd), f(N) = min lcm(d,e) over distinct d+e=N−1 (use 1 as third divisor). So g(c)=⌊2025!·lcm(d,e)/M⌋/2025!. Since M=3^{2025!}≫2025!·lcm, floor=0 unless lcm≥M/2025!. Find c where N−1 can be split into d,e with lcm≥M/2025! (i.e., d,e≈M). This occurs only when N odd ⇒ N−3 even ⇒ lcm(1,2)=2<… → all g(c)=0. Sum=0 ⇒ p/q=0/1 ⇒ p+q=1 ⇒ answer 1 mod 99991.

Insights: $f(N)$ is minimal $x$ with three distinct divisors summing to $N$. For $N=M+c$, use divisor $M$ (since $M=3^{2025!}$). Need $c$ as sum of two distinct divisors of $x$. If $c=3^a+3^b$ (a<b<K) then $x=M$ works → $f(N)=M$. Otherwise multiply $M$ by smallest $k$ giving two distinct divisors summing to $c$ (e.g., $k=2$ if $c$ needs a factor 2). Then $g(c)=\frac1{2025!}\lfloor2025!·f(N)/M\rfloor$ equals $1$ when $f(N)=M$, else equals $k$ when $f(N)=kM$ (since $2025!·kM/M=2025!·k$ integer). Compute $c$ values: 0, $4M$, 1848374, 10162574, 265710644, 44636594. Check each $c$ for representation as sum of two distinct powers of 3 (<K). If yes → $g=1$, else find minimal $k$ (likely 2). Sum $g$’s → rational $p/q$, then output $(p+q)\bmod99991$.

Insights: f(n)=min_{a<b<c, a+b+c=n} lcm(a,b,c). For any divisor d|n, f(n)=min_{d|n} d·g(n/d) where g(m)=min_{p+q+r=m} lcm(p,q,r). Hence f(n)/n = min_{m|n} g(m)/m.  

Compute g(m)/m for small m (≥6). Brute‑force shows the minimum ratio is 6/11 (from triple (2,3,6)), next 4/7≈0.571, then 3/5≈0.6, etc.  

Thus for any N, f(N)/N = min_{m|N} g(m)/m = min_{m|N} (ratio of m).  

M=3^{2025!}. Its divisors are powers of 3, so ratios considered are g(3^k)/3^k. For k≥2, g(3^k)/3^k = 4/7 (triple (3^{k-1},2·3^{k-1},4·3^{k-1})). For k=1, ratio=6/11 (since 3 not ≥6). Hence f(M)/M = 4/7.  

For N=M+4M=5M, divisors include 5 and powers of 3. Ratio min = min(4/7, g(5)/5). g(5)=? (no triple, n≥6) so ignore; thus f(5M)/5M = 4/7.  

For N=M+c with c not divisible by 3, only divisor 1, so f(N)/N = g(N)/N. Since N≈M huge, its minimal ratio equals the global minimum 6/11 (achieved when N is multiple of 11). The given c’s are chosen so M+c ≡0 (mod 11). Hence f(M+c)/ (M+c)=6/11 for those c.  

Thus f(M)= (4/7)M, f(5M)= (4/7)·5M, and for each other c, f(M+c)= (6/11)(M+c).  

Now g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025!. Compute:  

- c=0: f(M)=4M/7 ⇒ 2025!·f/M =2025!·4/7 ⇒ floor =2025!·4/7 (since 2025! divisible by 7? 2025! contains 7, so integer). ⇒ g(0)=4/7.  

- c=4M: N=5M, f=20M/7 ⇒ 2025!·20/7 ⇒ integer ⇒ g=20/7.  

- For each other c: f(N)=6(N)/11 ⇒ 2025!·6(N)/11M =2025!·6/11·(1 + c/M). Since c≪M, term c/M <1/2025! ⇒ floor =2025!·6/11 (no extra). ⇒ g(c)=6/11.  

Sum = 4/7 + 20/7 + 4·(6/11) = (24/7) + (24/11) = (24·11 + 24·7)/(77) = (264+168)/77 = 432/77 = p/q.  

Reduce: gcd(432,77)=1. p+q=432+77=509.  

Answer = 509 mod 99991 = **509**.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Minimal ratio LCM/n=6/11, achieved by (L/3,L/2,L) when n≡0 (mod 11). Since M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod 11), all n=M+c give n≡1,5,2,3 (mod 11) → not ≡0, so f(n)>6n/11. Use LCM≥6n/11 and find exact f for each n via divisor structure (L multiple of 6 gives ratio 6/11; otherwise next best ratio from L multiple of 2 or 3). Compute f(M+c)≈⌈6n/11⌉ or ⌈5n/9⌉ etc., then g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025!≈f/M. Sum g’s → rational p/q → output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure distinct divisors, handle rounding from floor, verify n mod 11 condition.

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) for distinct a+b+c=n. Minimal ratio lcm/n occurs when c divisible by 6, a=c/2,b=c/3 → ratio 6/11 (n=11t). If n≠0 (mod 11) next best is c divisible by 4, a=c/2,b=c/4 → ratio 4/7 (n=7t). For any n, f(n)=⌈(6/11)n⌉ if 11|n, else ⌈(4/7)n⌉ if 7|n, else larger. Compute M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod 11). For each c, check S=M+c mod 11,7 to decide which case applies, then f(S)=⌈ratio·S⌉. Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·f(S)/M⌋/2025!; sum floors, reduce to p/q, output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure distinct divisors (c/2≠c/3 etc.), handle non‑multiples correctly, use integer arithmetic for huge M via modular ratios.

Insights: f(N)=S−S/t where S=N−1 and t=smallest divisor ≥3 of S (if S composite); if S prime, f(N)=2S−4. For N≈M=3^{2025!}+c, M≡1 (mod d) for any d≤2026, d≠3, so S≡k+1 (mod d). Thus t is the smallest divisor of k+1 (≥3) unless 2 or 4 divide S. Results: c=0→t=4; c=1848374→t=11; c=265710644→t=4; c=44636594→t=17; c=10162574→k+1=10162574=2·5081287 ⇒ t=5081287; c=4M→S=5M−1, k+1=5·M, smallest divisor≥3 is 5 (since M≡0 mod 5? actually M≡1 mod 5, so S≡4 mod 5, check 7 etc). Compute t for 4M similarly. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·(t−1)/t⌋/2025! = (t−1)/t if t|2025! else 1−⌈2025!/t⌉/2025!. Sum the six g’s, reduce p/q, output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: handle prime‑S case (t=S) → g=1−1/2025!; ensure t>2025 may not divide 2025!. Use t from smallest divisor of k+1 (≥3) or from S=5M−1 analysis.

Insights: f(n)=min N with N+N/p+N/q=n (p,q>1 distinct, N divisible by p,q). Ratio r=pq/(pq+p+q). Need denominator b=(pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,pq+p+q) | n (n=M+c, M≡1 mod b). Test small (p,q): (2,3)→b=11,r=6/11; (2,4)→b=7,r=4/7; (2,5)→b=17,r=10/17; (2,6)→b=5,r=3/5; (2,7)→b=23,r=14/23; (2,8)→b=13,r=8/13; (2,9)→b=29,r=18/29; (2,10)→b=8,r=5/8; (3,6)→b=3,r=2/3; etc. For each c compute c mod b; smallest r with c≡−1 (mod b) (or c≡0 mod 3 for b=3) gives f(M+c)=r·(M+c). Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025! =⌊r·(M+c)/M⌋/2025! =⌊r·(1+c/M)⌋/2025!≈⌊r⌋/2025! (since c≪M). So g(c)=0 unless r≥1. All r<1 ⇒ floor=0 ⇒ g(c)=0. Hence sum=0 ⇒ p/q=0 ⇒ p+q=1 ⇒ answer 1 mod 99991. (Watch: ensure r<1 for all c.)

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ choose L=LCM, a,b|L, a+b=n−L. Write a=L/p, b=L/q (p<q). Then n=L(1+1/p+1/q) ⇒ L/n=R(p,q)=pq/[(p+1)(q+1)−1]. Need D′=( (p+1)(q+1)−1 )/gcd(pq,…) | n. Minimal R gives f(n)=R·n. Pre‑compute pairs (p,q) sorted by R, with required divisor D′ (e.g. (2,3):R=6/11,D′=11; (2,4):4/7,D′=7; (2,6):3/5,D′=5; …). For each n=M+c (M=3^{2025!}), compute M mod D′ (use 3^{2025!}≡1 mod any coprime D′, ≡0 if D′ has factor 3). Find smallest‑R pair whose D′ divides n. Then f(n)=R·n, g(c)=⌊2025!·f(n)/M⌋/2025!≈f(n)/M. Sum g’s → rational p/q; compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure a,b distinct (p≠q), D′|n (use gcd), handle large M via modular exponentiation (φ( D′ )).

Insights: f(n)=min N with 3 divisors sum n ⇒ N=n−1−d where d is largest proper divisor of S=n−1 (≠S/2). So p=smallest odd prime divisor of S, d=S/p, f(n)=(p−1)/p·S.  

Thus g(c)=⌊K·(p−1)(M+c−1)/(pM)⌋/K with K=2025!.  

For c≪M, δ=0 ⇒ g(c)=(p−1)/p−(p−(K mod p))/(pK).  

Compute p for each c:  

c=0 → S=M−1, p=5.  

c=1848374 → p=11.  

c=10162574 → p=5081287.  

c=265710644 → p=29.  

c=44636594 → p=17.  

c=4M → S=5M−1, smallest p=11549 (found by testing 5·3^{K}≡1 mod p).  

For c=4M, δ=1 (since (c−1)/M≈4) ⇒ g(4M)=5(p−1)/p−1/K.  

Sum all g’s, simplify to p/q, then compute (p+q) mod 99991.  

Pitfalls: ensure p>2025 ⇒ K mod p≠0, handle δ correctly (δ=1 only for c=4M). Use exact integer arithmetic for K·(p−1) etc.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)=n·min_{p<q}(pq/D) where D=(p+1)(q+1)−1 and D′=D/gcd(D,pq) must divide n. Ratio R=pq/D; smallest R’s: 6/11 (D′=11), 4/7 (7), 10/17 (17), 3/5 (5)… For n=M+c, M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod D′) (since 3^{2025!}≡1 mod any D′ not multiple of 3). Hence D′|n ⇔ D′|(c+1). So for each c compute divisors of c+1, find smallest D′ among {11,7,17,5,23,13,…} that divides c+1; the corresponding ratio R gives f(n)=R·n. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(n)/M⌋/2025! = R·(1+⌊c/M⌋) (c<M ⇒ g(c)=R; c=4M ⇒ g=5R). Sum the six R’s, express as p/q, output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure D′ list includes all needed (p,q up to enough size) and reduce R to lowest terms; M≡1 mod D′ holds because D′ not divisible by 3.

Insights: f(n)=min N with 1,d,N divisors ⇒ N=n−1−d where d is largest proper divisor of S=n−1 (≠S/2). So p=smallest odd prime|S, d=S/p, f(n)=(p−1)/p·S. For n=M+c (M=3^K, K=2025!), p_i = smallest odd prime dividing S_i=M+c−1. For c≪M, p_i = smallest odd prime divisor of c (or 5 for c=0). Compute p: c=0→5; 1848374→11; 10162574→5081287; 265710644→29; 44636594→17; c=4M→11549 (solve 5·3^K≡1 mod p). g(c)=⌊K·(p−1)(M+c−1)/(pM)⌋/K = (p−1)/p−(p−R)/(pK) (δ=0) for small c; for c=4M, g=5(p−1)/p+( {5R}/p−1)/K. Sum S = Σ(p_i−1)/p_i +5(p₁−1)/p₁ + correction/K. Compute K mod 99991, p_i,R_i, r=5R₁ mod p₁; then p+q≡? (final mod 99991). Pitfalls: ensure δ=0 for small c, handle large‑c case, use K mod 99991 (K≡0 mod 99991? since 99991<2025). Use modular inverses.

Insights: f(n) = min N>n/2 with divisors a,b (a=N/x,b=N/y) s.t. N+ a+ b=n. For small x,y, N=n·xy/(xy+x+y). Need D=xy+x+y, g=gcd(xy,D); require (D/g)|n. Since M≡1 (mod any D/g), condition ⇔ (c+1)≡0 (mod D/g). Test pairs (2,3),(2,4),(2,5)… in order of increasing N (ratio xy/D). If none work, use a=1 method: p=smallest odd divisor of n−1 (p=3 if c≡1 mod3 else smallest odd prime|c); N=((p−1)(n−1))/p. Compute N/M≈ratio r; g(c)=⌊2025!·r·(1+c/M)⌋/2025!. For c≠4M, floor≈⌊2025!·r⌋; for c=4M, floor≈⌊5·2025!·r⌋. Sum floors → p/q; answer (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: parity (x=2 needs N even), ensure N% x=y=0, D/g|n, handle c=4M separately.

Insights: f(n)=min c where ∃ distinct divisors a,b|c, a+b=n−c ⇒ c=n·pq/(pq+p+q) with p,q>1 distinct, d=(pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,pq+p+q) must divide n. Minimal ratio r=pq/(pq+p+q).  

Compute M=3^{2025!} (≡1 mod 11,7,5).  

For each S=M+c: test patterns (p,q) sorted by r: (2,3)→d=11 (needs S≡0 mod 11); (2,4)→d=7; (2,5)→d=17; (2,6)→d=5; (3,6)→d=3.  

M: only d=3 works →r=2/3.  

5M: d=5 works →r=3/5.  

M+offsets (offset≡4 mod 5) ⇒S≡0 mod 5 →r=3/5.  

Thus g’s: 2/3, five×3/5 → sum=2/3+3=11/3 →p+q=14 →14 mod 99991.

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) for a+b+c=n. Minimal ratio f(n)/n is 6/11 (n multiple of 11); next 4/7 (7), 10/17 (17), 3/5 (10), 8/13 (13), 14/23 (23), … For N=M+c (c≪M) divisors are those d|c+1 (since M≡1 mod d, d∤3). g(c)=f(N)/M≈f(N)/N=r(d) where d is smallest‑ratio divisor of N. Compute: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25 (d=25), g(10162574)=30/47 (d=47), g(265710644)=64/97 (d=97), g(44636594)=68/103 (d=103). Sum=4+16/25+30/47+64/97+68/103=77460082/11739425. (p+q) mod 99991 = 7535. Pitfalls: ensure M≡1 (mod d) for d coprime to 3; ignore 3‑powers (ratio 2/3). Use smallest‑ratio divisor, not just any.

Insights: f(n)=min c with distinct divisors a,b|c, a+b=n−c ⇒ c=n·pq/(pq+p+q) for integers p,q>1, D=(pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,D) must divide n. For M=3^{2025!}, M≡1 (mod D) for any D∤3. Check c+1≡0 (mod D). Smallest ratios: (2,3):6/11 (D=11), (2,4):4/7 (D=7), (2,6):3/5 (D=5), (3,6):2/3 (D=3). Compute S=M (D=3)⇒r=2/3; S=5M (D=5)⇒r=3/5→g=3; other S=M+offset (offset≡4 mod 5)⇒D=5⇒r=3/5. Sum=2/3+3+4·3/5=91/15 ⇒p+q=106.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)/n = min_{d|n} f(d)/d. Global minima: 6/11 (d=11), 4/7 (7), 10/17 (17), 3/5 (5), else 2/3 (3‑powers). For N=M+c (c≪M) M≡1 (mod d) for d≤2025, d∤3 ⇒ N≡0 (mod d) ⇔ (c+1)≡0 (mod d). Compute smallest d dividing c+1 from {11,7,17,5,…}. Then g(c)=f(d)/d·(1+⌊c/M⌋). Results: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum=125561848/19033825 ⇒ p+q≡7535 (mod 99991). Pitfalls: handle d=5 (c+1 multiple of 5) → ratio 3/5, c=4M case multiplies by 5. Ensure d≥6 and coprime to 3.

Insights: f(n)= (p‑1)/p·(n‑1) where p=smallest odd prime divisor of n‑1 (if n‑1 not a power of 2). For n=M+c (M=3^{2025!}) compute p for each c. Small c ⇒ p is smallest odd prime dividing c (or 5 for c=0). For c=4M, solve 5·3^{2025!}≡1 (mod p) → p=11549. Compute K=2025!. For p≤2025, K≡0 (mod p) → g(c)=(p‑1)/p. For p>2025, g(c)=(p‑1)/p‑(p‑R)/(pK) (R=K mod p). For c=4M, g=5(p‑1)/p+({5R/p}‑1)/K. Sum all g, combine fractions (denominator D=K·∏p). Reduce, then (p+q) mod 99991 = 40614. Pitfalls: don’t apply correction for p|K; handle c=4M separately; ensure reduction before mod.

Insights: f(N) = N·a/b where a/b = p·q/(pq+p+q) for some distinct p,q>1, with b = (pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,pq+p+q) dividing N and p|x,q|x (check via gcd). For N=M (3^K) only b=3 works → a/b=2/3. For N=5M, (p,q)=(3,6) gives a/b=2/3 → g(4M)=5·2/3=10/3. For N=M+c (c small) the minimal pair is (2,q) giving a/b=2q/(3q+2) where b=(3q+2)/gcd(3q+2,2q) divides N. Compute c mod b ⇒ find smallest q: c=1848374→q=16 (16/25), 10162574→q=15 (30/47), 265710644→q=64 (64/97), 44636594→q=55 (110/167). Sum =2/3+10/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167=125561848/19033825. p+q mod 99991 = 8687. Pitfalls: ensure p,q divide x (use factor_p = p/gcd(p,a) condition) and compute M mod b via CRT (M≡0 mod 3^e, ≡1 mod r).

Insights: f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N. For N=M+c (c≪M), M≡1 (mod d) for any d∤3, so pattern (p,q) works iff D′=(pq+p+q)/gcd(pq,D) |(c+1). Minimal ratio r=pq/D. Results: g(0)=2/3 (D′=3); g(4M)=3 (S=5M, D′=5, r=3/5 → floor gives 3); for each small c, D′=5 divides c+1, giving r=3/5. Sum=2/3+3+4·3/5=91/15 ⇒ p+q=106.

Insights: f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N ⇒ f(N)=r·N where r=min {f(d)/d | d|N, d≥6}. For N=M+c (c≪M) M≡1 (mod d) for any d coprime to 3, so d|N ⇔ d|(c+1). Compute r(d)=f(d)/d for small d (≤2025) via brute‑force; sorted by r: 6/11, 4/7, 10/17, 3/5, 8/13, 14/23,… For each c, find smallest d|c+1 (coprime to 3) giving minimal r. Results: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum = 125561848/19033825 ⇒ p+q≡8687 (mod 99991). Pitfalls: include only d≥6, ignore 3‑powers (N not divisible by 3), ensure denominator d|2025! so floor doesn’t affect.
